name: Numeri
desc: Numbers — the ones you'll actually use

vocabulary.note: Uno loses its -o before a noun: un cane, un amico — never “uno cane”. You're welcome.
Identical to “sei” = you are. Context saves you: “sei anni” (six years) vs “sei simpatico” (you're nice).
In Italy 13 is just a number. The unlucky one is 17, diciassette. Blame Roman numerals (XVII → VIXI, “I lived”).
Italians use the 24-hour clock: 15:00 = quindici. Miss a train appointment once and you'll never forget.
Dieci drops its last vowel: diciotto, NOT “dieciotto”. Same for diciannove.
Venti + uno → ventuno. The -i falls off before uno and otto: ventotto, not “ventiotto”.
Plural is “mila”: duemila, tremila. A thousand little irregularities, this language.

vocabulary.exEn: The book costs two hundred euros.
vocabulary.note: Cento never takes a plural — duecento, trecento, quattrocento… compound and done.

vocabulary.exEn: The car costs two thousand euros.
vocabulary.note: Mille turns into -mila when it teams up: duemila, tremila, diecimila. Never 'due mille'.

vocabulary.exEn: Hundreds of people at the party.
vocabulary.note: centinaio → centinaia, migliaio → migliaia. The 'di' is not optional.
Same pattern as centinaia — singular for the vague number, plural form for 'of them'.

vocabulary.ex: Un milione di euro, per favore.
vocabulary.note: Milione has a plural: due milioni. And it keeps its 'di': un milione di persone.

vocabulary.exEn: The company is worth a billion.
vocabulary.note: The classic trap: English 'billion' is miliardo, NOT 'bilione'. Bilione technically means a million millions and nobody uses it. Say miliardo.
Telling time out loud: le due e mezza, le tre e un quarto. Nobody says 'le 14:30' with their mouth.

vocabulary.exEn: I'd like half a pizza, please.
vocabulary.note: Before a noun: mezzo/mezza (mezzo litro, mezza pizza). On its own: la metà.

vocabulary.ex: Ho letto la metà del libro.
vocabulary.note: La metà di — 'half of'. Mezza pizza on the menu, la metà when you're bragging about progress.

vocabulary.ex: Ci vuole il doppio del tempo.
vocabulary.note: Il doppio di — 'double the'. Works for time, quantities, and excuses.

vocabulary.exEn: We were about twenty or so.
vocabulary.note: Can float after the number too: 'venti persone circa'. Very Italian vagueness.

vocabulary.ex: Ci vediamo tra un paio di giorni.
vocabulary.exEn: See you in a couple of days.
vocabulary.note: 'Un paio di' is delightfully vague — could be two, could be five. Nobody counts.
